content.text: Audit complete. `findings.json` is written at the repo root (the only file I created or touched). ## What I reviewed All first-party code — the `impl/` core (tokenizer, parser, generator, reader/writer, pointer/patch/merge-patch, builders, context/config, 7.2k LoC), the `rest/` JAX-RS media providers, `demos/*`, `providers/*`, and the CI workflow. Third-party deps ignored. No network access, so I couldn't diff against upstream Maven artifacts; review was manual. ## Finding (1) **CWE-79 — XSS in `demos/rest/.../ParserResource.java:73-74`** (`writeFlickerFeed`) The resource is `@Produces("text/html")` and is registered in `DemoApplication`. It fetches JSON over **cleartext `http://api.flickr.com/...`** and concatenates the parsed `id`/`server`/`secret`/`farm` string values directly into an `` tag with no attribute encoding or validation. An on-path attacker (or attacker-influenced upstream content) who sets e.g. `farm` to `4" onerror="alert(document.cookie)" x="` gets script execution in the app's origin. Source→sink path is included in the JSON. ## In-scope categories with no findings - **SQL/command/code/template injection:** no `Runtime`/`ProcessBuilder`/JDBC/template engines anywhere. - **Path traversal:** no filesystem access in main code; `JsonPointerImpl` splits on `/` *before* unescaping `~0`/`~1`, so escaped separators can't create extra path segments, and `JsonPatchImpl` keeps the RFC 6902 `move` proper-prefix check. - **SSRF:** every URL in the repo is a hardcoded constant; no request data reaches a URL. - **Insecure deserialization:** the only `ObjectInputStream` use is a test round-tripping its own bytes. - **XXE:** no XML parsing in the project at all. - **Auth/authz bypass:** no authentication or access-control logic exists. I also verified the parser's hardening is intact (`maxDepth` enforced in `JsonParserImpl.Stack.push`, `maxBigDecimalLength` in `JsonTokenizer.getBigDecimal`, `maxBigIntegerScale` in `JsonNumberImpl.bigIntegerValue`), and that `writeEscapedString`/`JsonStringImpl.toString` escape quotes, backslashes and control characters correctly, so untrusted strings can't break out of generated JSON. ## Two things I deliberately left out of `findings.json` Both are real but outside the vulnerability classes you scoped: 1. **Infinite loop (CWE-835, availability):** `JsonParserImpl.ObjectContext.skip()` (line 534) and `ArrayContext.skip()` (line 594) loop until a matching close token; on truncated input the tokenizer returns `EOF` forever, so an app calling `skipObject()`/`skipArray()` on `{"a":{` spins indefinitely. 2. **Hardcoded Flickr API key (CWE-798) and cleartext HTTP** in the same demo file (line 53) — the missing TLS is what makes finding 1 practically exploitable, so it's described inside that explanation.
